To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatial resolution of location requests can be adapted to provide anonymity, and that the spatial resolution required for anonymity in urban areas is similar to the resolution currently required for E-911 service.

the median resolution of location-based services for urban areas can be adjusted to meet specified anonymity requirements and that the median resolution for anonymity requirements of 1000 and 10000 is about 125 and 250 meters, respectively.

(1) we present a middleware architecture and adaptive algorithms that can be deployed to provide anonymous location-based services; and (2) we estimate the expected spatial resolution of location information that is needed to achieve a desired degree of anonymity in urban areas, and find it to be 125 meters, the current accuracy needed for E- 911 services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of an anonymity-preserving location-based service.
the question: How much information is required to provide anonymous location-based services?
the problem of how to guarantee the anonymity of users of location-based services, while providing sufficient resolution to support useful location-based applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial and temporal cloaking techniques proposed in this paper can be implemented in real-time and can provide sufficient resolution for a wide range of location-based services.
the spatial resolution of location information is a function of the number of people in the vicinity of the user, the number of service providers, the number of users and the anonymity constraints.
the proposed system can guarantee anonymity for a user who requests a location-based service, and that the system is able to adapt to the changing conditions of the user environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed algorithms and a prototype implementation for a location broker service which can provide anonymous location information to location-based services, while maintaining a reasonable resolution.
our algorithms are able to provide a reasonable level of anonymity for location services while still maintaining a high enough spatial and temporal resolution for most applications.
the proposed architecture can be used for anonymous location-based services with reasonable accuracy and low computational complexity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve anonymity for users of location services without sacrificing the utility of location-based services.
it is possible to provide anonymous location-based services without significantly compromising the utility of the location information.
anonymity is achievable with current technologies.
